title: Stakeholder Conversation: diagnose your three questions
description: Use AI follow-up questions to find out which of your three validation questions would help you listen, and which pitch your own idea.

questions.prompt: Paste the three validation questions you are bringing from your Stakeholder Map, the stakeholder you have chosen and their relationship to the problem, what you hope to learn from each question, and the single assumption this conversation is meant to test.
questions.placeholder: Bring the questions from your assumption blocks rather than writing new ones. Include the stakeholder's relationship to the problem, what each question is meant to test, and the one assumption this conversation is built around.
questions.aiContext: This is Sprint 3 of Reframing Problems with AI. The participant is preparing three questions for a real conversation with a real stakeholder, and the questions come from assumption blocks they already wrote. Diagnose each question as leading, vague, or missing evidence, and say which one it is and why. Leading means it nudges the stakeholder toward the answer they want. Vague means it is unclear what is being asked, so any answer would be hard to use. Missing evidence means it asks for an opinion rather than something verifiable, such as an experience, a specific example, or a real decision the stakeholder made. Do not rewrite the questions; the participant rewrites them. Push them to check that each question is answerable by the specific person they chose, that the three questions test the named assumption rather than three unrelated things, and that they are listening rather than seeking approval for a solution they already have in mind.
questions.discussionPrompt: Use these questions to rewrite the weak ones yourself, then update Section A of your report.
questions.summaryPlaceholder: Write the three questions you will actually ask, each with what you hope to learn from it, and name the assumption this conversation tests.
